Scaly blepharitis


Treatment

  • General TTT: TTT of predisposing factors & associated conditions.

  • Local TTT: Lid hygiene using:

    • Warm compresses, Eyelid massage.

    • Removal of scales using diluted solution of baby shampoo.

    • Local antibiotic ointment.

Parasitic blepharitis

  • C.O: Infestation by Pubic crab louse and its ova

Zeis glands

Treatment

  • -TTT of the predisposing factors.

  • -Warm, moist compresses and topical antibiotics (drops and ointment).

  • -Systemic antibiotics are indicated in severe cases, complicated by cellulites.

  • -If Pointing: drain pus by epilation of the related eye lash with a horizontal incision.

  • -Do not press to evacuate a stye (dangerous area) may spread infection and cause orbital cellulites or cavernous sinus thrombosis.

  • -Infected chalazion has Same TTT for stye, but evacuation may be needed through a vertical or cruciate incision on the conjunctival side.

Chalazion meibomian gland 

Treatment:

  • -Small chalazion: may be left alone with follow up.

  • -Large chalazion: incision (cruciate or vertical) and curettage or scraping of its contents from the conjunctival side

  • -Infected chalazion: As hordeolum internum.

  • -Recurrent swelling in the same gland: Excision biopsy and histopathological examination is done to exclude malignancy

Trichiasis
Def: His an acquired condition in which more than 4 lashes are directed posteriorly and rub against the cornea or bulbar conjunctiva

Distichiasis
Def: an abnormality (usually congenital) in which extra raw of lashes arise from the lid margin behind the grey line in the place of Meibomian gland orifices.

Trichiasis

Complications:

  • -Chronic conjunctivitis, conjunctival ulceration & epithelial plaque.

  • -Corneal: recurrent ulceration which may be followed by opacification, superficial vascularization & epithelial plaque.

Cicatracial entropion

Causes

  1. 1-Trachoma (the commonest cause in Egypt)

  2. 2-Ulcerative blepharitis.

  3. 3-Trauma and Chemical burns.

  4. 4-Cicatrizing diseases: ocular cicatricial pemphigoid and Stevens Johnson disease.

Involutional ectropion

Mechanism: 

-due to age related degeneration of elastic tissue within the eyelid leading to horizontal laxity . 

-Overriding of pre-tarsal over pre-septal orbicularis oculi and vertical eyelid instability due to weak or dis-inserted lower eyelid retractors are contributing factors.

Cicatracial ectropion

Treatment

  • -Protect the cornea from exposure until the deformity is corrected surgically by:

  • 1-Small scar: V-Y operation.

  • 2-Large scar: removal of the scar tissue followed by eyelid grafting.
